tw-mi-grand-haven-light-house-hill-convi.st: The Grand Rapids Press (11 Oct 1899) put Baty's first dig 'at the very pinnacle of Five Mile Hill', 'back of the lighthouse', with a team and scraper down 12-15 ft and aiming for 30-40 ft, guided by a $125 'instrument'; it said the pot was 'said to be worth $60,000'.

tw-mi-wabasis-lake-gold.t: The Grand Haven Tribune (19 Apr 1900) says the Five Mile Hill digger Baty came from a treasure hunt at 'Wabassee Lake', Kent Co., in fall 1899, so the kettle was being dug for by 1899.

tw-ia-dubuque-kelly-bluff.st: A 1936 WPA 'Iowa Oddities' piece lists four finds on the bluff: a $10,000 iron chest (Geiger and Becke), a $1,200 can (the boy Peter Fortune), an $1,800 small chest (a youth named Reynolds) and $500 found by workmen digging a reservoir on the old claim in 1914. It says a large iron chest Kelly had a Dubuque blacksmith forge (2 ft 10 in x 32 in x 8 in) has never been found and is believed to hold most of the fortune, and that augers were still probing in 1936. It gives his death as 15 May 1859; the card keeps 1867 from the 1868 papers.
src: Des Moines Register, 19 Apr 1936, p. 48, WPA 'Iowa Oddities' (August Lenox) (Newspapers.com 130604521)

m-tr-rc-2.st: The Escanaba Daily Press (6 Feb 1937) adds that the liquor was kept in a cave reached by a tunnel from the saloon, and dates the Milwaukee man's visit about 1912.

set.st: Peter Whitmore ("Old Whit") Knaggs, keeper of the Shiawassee post from 1820 (d. 1848 at Toledo; his wife Catherine Visger died at the post in 1835), kept a trading post and was said to have gathered gold from land speculators; he buried it along the Shiawassee River just south of Knaggs' Bridge. Pin is approximate, not the spot itself. Knaggs' hill is on the E (right) bank; Gaylord Cemetery adjoins it: look-only near the cemetery. 1873 atlas places the crossing beside the Shiawassee treaty reserve. 1936: Knaggs gully near the bridge, dug over many times. The earliest telling found (Michigan Pioneer and Historical Collections, 1902) says Whitmore Knaggs buried speculators' money around Knaggs Bridge on the Shiawassee. A man named Hadd dug for it about twenty years later, and before the Civil War parties dug at night by a map that marked 'the rock, the tree, and the spring' (E. O. Byam showed them the spring). It names storekeeper Thomas B. Allen, and says the post site then belonged to Hon. N. G. Phillips. The 1906 county history ('Shiawassee's Captain Kidd') adds that the searchers asked after 'a rock in the river known as Indian Rock'; no Indian Rock is named in GNIS, and the rock is not yet located.
set.n: Peter Whitmore Knaggs' gold, Shiawassee River south of Knaggs Bridge
